directAnswer: Pope Clement II (reigned 1046–1047), born Suidger, was the bishop of Bamberg chosen by King Henry III at the Council of Sutri. On the day of his consecration, Christmas 1046, he crowned Henry emperor. He held a synod against simony, died within ten months, and is the only pope buried north of the Alps.

sections.h2: Suidger, Saxon Noble and Bishop of Bamberg
paras: Suidger was born into a noble Saxon family, traditionally associated with Hornburg in Saxony. He served as a canon at Halberstadt and in the royal chapel before Henry III appointed him bishop of Bamberg in 1040. He accompanied Henry on his journey to Italy in 1046.

sections.h2: Elected at Sutri, Consecrated at Christmas
paras: After the Council of Sutri removed Gregory VI, and Benedict IX and Sylvester III were set aside, Henry III proposed Suidger as pope. The Roman clergy and people accepted him, and he took the name Clement. He was consecrated on Christmas Day 1046, and on the same day he crowned Henry III and Queen Agnes as emperor and empress.
Clement kept his bishopric of Bamberg, a sign of his close attachment to the German church and to Henry's circle.

In January 1047 Clement held a synod in Rome that condemned simony and imposed penalties on those who had knowingly received ordination from simoniac bishops. The decrees signaled the beginning of a period of German reforming popes who would transform the papacy over the following decades. Clement also canonized Wiborada, a recluse of St. Gall killed during a Magyar raid in 926.

He was the first of a line of popes from the German lands chosen with Henry III's backing, followed by Damasus II, Leo IX and Victor II. Together they turned the papacy from a prize of Roman families into the driving force of church reform.

sections.h2: Death and a Grave in Bamberg
paras: Clement died on 9 October 1047 at the monastery of San Tommaso near Pesaro, after less than a year in office. His body was taken to Bamberg and buried in the cathedral, making him the only pope buried in Germany, indeed north of the Alps.

Rumors that he had been poisoned circulated at the time. A twentieth-century examination of his remains reportedly found high levels of lead, which some have read as support for poisoning, though the evidence is not conclusive. After his death, Benedict IX returned to Rome for a third time.

keyFacts: Born Suidger, a Saxon noble; bishop of Bamberg from 1040
Chosen by Henry III at the Council of Sutri
Crowned Henry III emperor on Christmas Day 1046
Held a synod against simony in January 1047
Buried in Bamberg Cathedral, the only papal tomb north of the Alps

faqs.question: Where is Pope Clement II buried?
faqs.answer: He is buried in Bamberg Cathedral in Germany, the only pope whose tomb lies north of the Alps.

faqs.question: Was Clement II poisoned?
faqs.answer: Contemporaries suspected it, and a twentieth-century study of his remains reportedly found high lead levels, but the cause of his death cannot be established with certainty.

faqs.question: Why did Clement II keep his bishopric of Bamberg?
faqs.answer: He remained deeply tied to the German church and Henry III's court, and he retained Bamberg alongside the papacy for his short reign.
